name: Himeji
ground: A hill on the road west out of the capital. Flat country around it, so the defence has to be in the plan rather than in the ground.

motte.note: A stone base, battered, curving outward at the foot — the curve sheds an earthquake rather than resisting it.

keep.name: The great keep
keep.note: Six storeys reading as five from outside. Whitewashed against fire.

wards.name: Hon-maru
wards.note: The first circle, at the top of the spiral.

axis.name: The spiral approach
axis.note: The path to the keep winds through twenty-one gates and doubles back repeatedly. It is longer than the castle is wide by a factor of ten, and every metre of it is overlooked.

figures.value: deliberately confusing — a spiral, not a line
the 1945 bombing and the 1995 Kobe earthquake

lesson: Where Krak makes you go through the wall, Himeji makes you go the long way. The approach is the weapon: a spiral turns an assault into a queue, and a queue can be dealt with a few at a time. If you cannot make the wall thicker, make the route longer.
